newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BIL keeps listing after CCB/CLF link.
newsitem.headline: BIL keeps listing after CCB/CLF link.

text.p: Banque Internationale a Luxembourg (BIL) will remain a separately-listed entity focusing on private banking once its controlling shareholder Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) and Credit Local de France link up, CCB said on Monday.
"BIL will remain within the alliance specialised in private banking in a large sense," CCB chief executive officer Francois Narmon said. CCB owns 52 percent of the Luxembourg bank.
"CCB and CLF will present themselves outside their domestic markets as one group called Dexia...BIL however will continue to present itself internationally as BIL," Narmon told reporters.
Narmon was speaking after CCB shareholders overwhelmingly approved the bank's planned alliance with CLF, which will create Europe's 22nd largest banking group, baptised Dexia.
Under the plan each parent company will set up a holding company in order to take a 50 percent stake in the partner's operational banks, which will keep their present names.

CCB Holding will remain in the grip of the bank's municipal shareholders, but between 25 and 30 percent ot its capital will be sold to institutional and retail investors in an initial public offering on the Brussels bourse next month.
CLF Holding will continue to be owned by the French government and CLF's existing public and private shareholders, who approved the planned alliance last week.
